Replying to @naomi when pricing my pieces I consider time spent making/decorating/signing/waxing/glazing/sanding/lustering/firing/invetorying. I have done time studies to help gauge the time I spend on making the pieces. I also consider materials used. I apply gold luster to almost every piece and it’s expensive and requires an additional firing which is also another expense. I also consider experience. I have been working with clay for 14 years now so I consider all of those years of working to this point in my pieces value as well. Pricing is hard! Placing a value on your art is uncomfortable. I’m just happy to be here and I’m doing my best with the knowledge I have gained so far on this journey. I don’t think there is a right answer that will work for everyone, I’m just trying to do what feels right to me! Thank you for reading! 💗💗💗💗 #wheelthrown #ceramics #sliptrailing #potterytiktok #porcelain

This piece of functional art is here to remind you that no matter how gloopy and messy life gets, there is always love and joy bursting through. 🌈💗 I am so excited to finally start sharing the first pieces from my 2026 collection! The first half of this year has been full of learning, experimenting, and pushing my work in new directions. It has also been one of the heaviest seasons of my life. While making this collection, I found myself returning again and again to the same idea: choosing hope. This piece feels like a little celebration of that. A reminder that even when things feel overwhelming, beautiful things can still emerge from the mess. Thankfully, the scary chapter my chosen family has been living through is coming to a very happy ending, and I am sitting in deep gratitude for that. Not everyone gets that outcome, and I don’t take it for granted for a second. videos.caption: pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

When pulling larger amounts of clay we need to stop and think of the limitations of our material alongside the additional weight. Pulling a cylinder on 1-3lbs of clay is different from pulling a cylinder on 5+lbs of clay. This is due to the immense amount of weight that is being supported by base of our vessel. If we thin out this base too early on we risk failure due to collapse. These thin walls at the bottom of the vessel struggle to support the weight above it in conjunction with the force caused by the centrifugal force of the wheel when moving it. To resolve this issue we must begin or first pull higher up the vessel. I choose to begin at the middle with my first pull to even out this weight and force. Then move my way back down to the bottom. #harleyweiglestudio #potterytutorials
